question: H1
answer:
ANSWER

A US airline operating under 14 CFR Part 121 must give a flight attendant a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours between the completion of one scheduled duty period and the start of the next, when the duty period is 14 hours or less. Ten consecutive hours is the baseline, standard-case answer.

GOVERNING AUTHORITY

14 CFR § 121.467, 'Flight attendant duty period limitations and rest requirements: Domestic, flag, and supplemental operations' (Part 121, Subpart P). This covers domestic, flag, and supplemental operations — i.e., essentially all Part 121 passenger flying — so the answer does not change between domestic and international (flag) flying for this provision.

Controlling text, § 121.467(b)(2): 'A flight attendant scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less as provided under paragraph (b)(1) of this section must be given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours. This rest period must occur between the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period.'

THE FULL REST MATRIX (all figures from the current rule text)

| Scheduled duty period | Required rest between duty periods | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| 14 hours or less | 10 consecutive hours, scheduled | § 121.467(b)(2) |
| More than 14, up to 20 hours | 12 consecutive hours, scheduled | § 121.467(b)(7) |
| More than 14, up to 20 hours, with the (b)(8) reduction elected | 10 consecutive hours (reduced), conditioned — see below | § 121.467(b)(8) |

Reduced-rest conditions under § 121.467(b)(8) and (b)(9) — all three must hold:
1. The flight attendant is given a subsequent rest period of at least 14 consecutive hours.
2. That subsequent 14-hour rest must be scheduled to begin no later than 24 hours after the beginning of the reduced 10-hour rest.
3. The certificate holder may not schedule that flight attendant for a duty period of more than 14 hours during the 24-hour period commencing after the beginning of the reduced rest period.

The floor never drops below 10 consecutive hours under the current rule. There is no 9-hour or 8-hour option.

ENFORCEMENT HOOKS

- § 121.467(b)(10): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant any duty period unless the flight attendant 'has had at least the minimum rest required under this section.' Note the 'has had' — this is the actual-rest gate, distinct from the 'scheduled rest' language of (b)(2). It is what makes a compressed-by-delay night a compliance issue, not merely a scheduling one.
- § 121.467(b)(11): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant to perform any duty during a required rest period. Rest must be duty-free.
- Paragraph (c) is the relief valve (the section opens 'Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section'). Its full text was not retrieved here; do not assume it licenses routine scheduling below 10 hours. Treat any reliance on (c) as requiring the carrier's ops/crew-scheduling and legal review against the current rule text.

HOW TO COMPUTE IT IN PRACTICE

1. Identify the scheduled duty period: release time minus report time for the assignment involving flight time ('duty period' is defined in Subpart P as the elapsed time between reporting for an assignment involving flight time and release from that assignment).
2. If that period is 14:00 or less, the next report time must be no earlier than release + 10:00.
3. If it exceeds 14:00 (up to 20:00), the next report must be no earlier than release + 12:00, unless the (b)(8) reduction is deliberately used — in which case release + 10:00 is allowed only with a 14-hour subsequent rest beginning within 24 hours of the start of the reduced rest, and a 14-hour duty cap in that 24-hour window.
4. Rest is measured from release from the scheduled duty period to report for the subsequent duty period — not from block-in, not from hotel arrival, and not from the end of flight time.
5. Verify the pairing actually delivers the number after all scheduled ground/deadhead segments; deadhead and ground time inside a duty period count against the duty period, not toward rest.

SOURCE CONFLICT — DISCLOSED AND RESOLVED

The FAA's public FAQ page ('What are the flight attendant duty period and rest requirements?') states nine consecutive hours, reducible to eight with a 10-hour subsequent rest beginning within 24 hours. That is the pre-2022 standard and is superseded. I relied on the current eCFR text of § 121.467(b)(2), (b)(7), (b)(8), (b)(9) — three independent fetches returning identical language — corroborated by the FAA's own final rule document 'Flight Attendant Duty Period Limitations and Rest Requirements' (ARM-220928-001), which implements FAARA 2018 § 335's mandate for 'at least 10 hours of consecutive rest,' and by the CFR volume citing Amdt. 121-386, 87 FR 61465 (Oct. 4, 2022). The rule text governs over a descriptive web page and over an earlier edition. If any internal document, training deck, or scheduling manual in your organization still shows 9/8 hours, it is out of date and should be corrected.

SCOPE LIMITS — WHAT THIS NUMBER IS AND IS NOT

- It is the federal regulatory floor for scheduled rest between duty periods. Collective bargaining agreements (e.g., AFA carrier agreements) and any applicable state law can be more protective; those figures are carrier-specific, were not sourced in the material reviewed, and are not stated here. Contract rest must be checked against the applicable agreement, not against this memo.
- It is a safety/rest rule, not a wage-and-hour rule. Whether rest is paid is a compensation question outside this provision.
- It addresses rest between duty periods. It does not set layover free time, monthly/hourly flight-time limits, or cumulative fatigue limits, which live elsewhere in Part 121 and in carrier policy.
- Currency: verified against eCFR as fetched 2026-11-15. Re-verify § 121.467 before relying on it in an enforcement-sensitive context.

ONE-LINE ANSWER FOR THE RECORD

Ten consecutive hours of scheduled, duty-free rest between duty periods — twelve if the preceding scheduled duty period exceeded 14 hours (up to 20), with a conditioned reduction back to ten only under § 121.467(b)(8).

question: H1
answer:
ANSWER

A US airline operating under 14 CFR Part 121 (domestic, flag, or supplemental operations) must give a flight attendant a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours between the completion of one scheduled duty period and the commencement of the next, when the duty period is 14 hours or less. 10 consecutive hours is the regulatory floor; there is no provision in Part 121 that permits a carrier to go below 10 hours.

GOVERNING AUTHORITY

14 CFR § 121.467 — 'Flight attendant duty period limitations and rest requirements: Domestic, flag, and supplemental operations,' current eCFR text, plus the FAA final rule implementing section 335(a) of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 (ARM-220928-001, 4 Oct 2022).

- § 121.467(b)(2): 'A flight attendant scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less ... must be given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours. This rest period must occur between the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period.'
- § 121.467(b)(10): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant any duty period unless the flight attendant has had at least the minimum rest required by the section.
- § 121.467(b)(11): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant to perform any duty during any required rest period.

FULL REST TABLE (Part 121)

| Scheduled duty period | Required scheduled rest | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| 14 hours or less | 10 consecutive hours (floor; not reducible) | § 121.467(b)(2) |
| More than 14 but not more than 20 hours | 12 consecutive hours | § 121.467(b)(7) |
| More than 14 but not more than 20 hours, with a subsequent rest of at least 14 consecutive hours beginning no later than 24 hours after the start of the reduced rest | may be reduced to 10 consecutive hours | § 121.467(b)(8) |

If the carrier uses the (b)(8) reduction, § 121.467(b)(9) prohibits scheduling that flight attendant for a duty period of more than 14 hours during the 24-hour period commencing after the beginning of the reduced rest period. In every Part 121 case the rest actually given is therefore at least 10 consecutive hours — that is the single number to plan to.

SCOPE AND CAVEATS

1. Part 121 only. Part 135 (§ 135.273) and Part 91 (§ 91.1062) still read 9 consecutive hours, reducible to 8 with a subsequent 10-hour rest. Those figures do not apply to a scheduled passenger carrier operating under Part 121, and they are not the answer to this question.
2. Measured on scheduled time. The rule is framed in terms of the 'scheduled' rest period between the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period. Actual operational delays do not shorten the requirement; they push the next duty period.
3. 'Duty period' includes release from safety of air carrier operations (i.e., debrief/paperwork), so the rest clock starts at release, not at block-in.
4. This is the federal legal minimum. Collective bargaining agreements (e.g., AFA) routinely provide more — commonly 11 to 12 hours, plus hotel and transportation provisions. Contractual rest is enforceable as a contract matter but is not the FAA minimum; the FAA rule is the answer to 'how much must the airline give.'
5. § 121.467 does not itself mandate hotel accommodations; it mandates the rest period and prohibits duty during it. Lodging and transport obligations generally arise from the contract and from the carrier's ops specs/manuals.
6. International flying by a US carrier remains subject to § 121.467 as the home-state minimum; host-country or bilateral requirements may add to it but cannot reduce it below 10 hours for a Part 121 carrier.

SOURCE DISCREPANCY — DISCLOSED AND RESOLVED

The FAA FAQ page 'What are the flight attendant duty period and rest requirements?' states nine consecutive hours, reducible to eight with a subsequent 10-hour rest. That text is stale: it reproduces the pre-2022 rule. It contradicts (a) the current eCFR text of § 121.467(b)(2) and (b) the FAA's own 2022 final rule, which requires 'at least 10 consecutive hours' and states the rest period is 'not reduced under any circumstances' for duty periods of 14 hours or less. Per the rule that the current edition of the rule text governs over a page describing it, the 10-hour figure controls. Where the two texts give different figures for the same thing, the current eCFR text and the final rule were relied on, and the FAQ's 9/8 figures should be treated as superseded.

COMPLIANCE CHECK FOR AN OPERATOR

For each pairing of consecutive duty periods, verify: (rest start) = release from duty per the duty-period definition; (rest end) = report for the next duty period; rest end minus rest start ≥ 10:00 for any preceding duty of ≤14:00; ≥ 12:00 for a preceding duty of >14:00 and ≤20:00, unless a ≥14:00 subsequent rest is scheduled to begin within 24:00 of the start of the reduced rest and no >14:00 duty is scheduled in that 24-hour window; no duty of any kind (including deadhead assignments that constitute duty, training, or office work) is assigned during the rest period.

question: H1
answer:
ANSWER — MINIMUM REST BETWEEN DUTY DAYS FOR A US AIRLINE FLIGHT ATTENDANT

Base value: 10 consecutive hours. Unit: hours. Scope: US domastic/flag/supplemental air carrier (14 CFR Part 121), cabin crewmember, scheduled rest between consecutive scheduled duty periods.

1. CONTROLLING RULE
14 CFR §121.467 (Flight attendant duty period limitations and rest requirements: Domestic, flag, and supplemental operations), Subpart P. Current eCFR text as fetched 2026-11-15.

§121.467(b)(2): 'A flight attendant scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less as provided under paragraph (b)(1) of this section must be given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours. This rest period must occur between the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period.'

So: 10 consecutive hours is the regulatory floor for the ordinary case (duty period of 14 hours or less), and it is owed by the certificate holder, not merely by contract.

2. FULL REST TABLE UNDER §121.467 — READ THE NUMBER IN CONTEXT
| Scheduled duty period | Required scheduled rest | Citation |
| 14 h or less | 10 consecutive hours | (b)(2) |
| More than 14 h but not more than 20 h | 12 consecutive hours | (b)(7) |
| Same as above, reduced rest election | 12 may be scheduled or reduced to 10 consecutive hours, provided a subsequent rest period of at least 14 consecutive hours, scheduled to begin no later than 24 hours after the beginning of the reduced rest period | (b)(8) |
| After any reduced rest to 10 h | No duty period of more than 14 h during the 24-hour period commencing after the beginning of the reduced rest period | (b)(9) |

Consistency check: every branch of the rule is at least 10 hours, so the stated headline figure of 10 does not violate any threshold set by the same rule; the 12-hour figure is a stricter case, and the reduced-rest path never goes below 10 for a Part 121 carrier.

3. TWO ENFORCEMENT PROVISIONS THAT MAKE THE 10 HOURS HARD, NOT ASPIRATIONAL
- §121.467(b)(10): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant any duty period unless the flight attendant has had at least the minimum rest required under the section.
- §121.467(b)(11): no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant to perform any duty during any required rest period.
Practical translation for a scheduler: the 10 hours is a block that cannot be encroched — no deadhead, no training, no phone-availability duty, no paperwork inside it.

4. WHAT 'BETWEEN DUTY DAYS' MEANS UNDER THE RULE
Duty day = the scheduled duty period. The rule's own words tie the rest to 'the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period' — not to actual release and actual report. Two consequences a compliance reviewer should record:
- The rest obligation is a scheduled-rest rule: a carrier complies by publishing pairings/schedules with at least 10 consecutive duty-free hours between scheduled duty periods.
- If actual duty runs long, the rule does not silently shorten the required rest; (b)(10) independently bars assigning the next duty period unless the minimum rest has in fact been had. Do not read (b)(2) as an 'actual rest' formula.

5. DISCREPANCY IN THE FETCHED TEXTS — STATED AND RESOLVED
The fetched pages show three different rest numbers for flight attendants:
- §121.467(b)(2): 10 consecutive hours (reducible path floored at 10 under (b)(8)).
- §135.273(b)(2): 9 consecutive hours, reducible to 8 under (b)(3) with a 10-hour compensatory rest.
- §91.1062(a)(2): 9 consecutive hours, reducible to 8 under (a)(3) with a 10-hour compensatory rest.
Which was relied on and why: §121.467. The ask is about a 'US airline' — a certificate holder conducting domastic, flag, or supplemental operations, which is Part 121. Part 135 governs commuter and on-demand operations and Part 91 subpart K governs program managers; their 9/8 figures do not apply to a Part 121 air carrier's flight attendants. The 9-hour and 8-hour figures should not be quoted to an airline without the Part 135/Part 91 qualifier.

6. WORKED EXAMPLES (ARITHMETIC CHECKED)
- Ordinary case: scheduled duty period ends 21:00. Earliest permissible report for the next scheduled duty period = 07:00 next day (21:00 + 10 h).
- Long-duty case: scheduled duty period of 15 h ends 21:00. Required rest = 12 h → earliest report 09:00 next day (21:00 + 12 h).
- Reduced-rest case: 12-h rest scheduled down to 10 h starting 22:00 on Day 1 (rest ends 08:00 Day 2). The carrier must then give a subsequent rest period of at least 14 consecutive hours beginning no later than 22:00 on Day 2 (24 h after the beginning of the reduced rest), and must not schedule that flight attendant for any duty period of more than 14 h in the 24 hours commencing 22:00 Day 1.

7. WHAT THIS ANSWER DOES NOT COVER (BOUNDARIES OF THE GRONDING, NOT BLOCKERS)
- Collective bargening agreements and carrier policy routinely set rest above 10 h (often 11-12 h, and higher for international or augmented creows). The question asked for the regulatory minimum, which is 10 h; contract figures are additive, never subtractive.
- §121.467(c) is referenced as an exception ('Except as provided in paragraph (c)') but its content is not in the fetched text; treat any (c)-based deviation as requiring verification against the current eCFR before use.
- Reserve/standby: the fetched text of §121.467 contains no reserve-specific rest provision. Whether standby counts as duty for the 14-h/10-h calculation is not resolved by these pages and should be verified separately.
- The fetched text of §121.467 imposes no express 'suitable accommodation' quality standard on the 10 hours; do not attribute one to it.
- Foreign jurisdictions' rules on flights touching their territory are outside this answer; the FAA rule above is the US carrier's own obligation.

8. ONE-LINE COMPLIANCE SUMMARY FOR THE SCHEDULE FILE
'Part 121 flight attendants receive at least 10 consecutive hours of scheduled, duty-free rest between the completion of one scheduled duty period and the commencement of the next; 12 consecutive hours when the scheduled duty period exceeds 14 hours, with a permitted reduction to 10 only when followed by at least 14 consecutive hours of compensatory rest beginning within 24 hours and with no duty period over 14 hours in the interim.'

question: H1
answer:
COMPLIANCE DETERMINATION — Minimum rest between duty periods for a US airline flight attendant

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER (regulatory floor, 14 CFR Part 121)
=====================================================================

For a US airline operating under 14 CFR Part 121 (domestic, flag, or supplemental operations), the minimum rest a certificate holder must give a flight attendant between duty periods is:

  **10 consecutive hours** — where the flight attendant is scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less. 14 CFR §121.467(b)(2).

  **12 consecutive hours** — where the flight attendant is scheduled to a duty period of more than 14 hours but not more than 20 hours. 14 CFR §121.467(b)(7).

  **10 consecutive hours** (reduced rest) — permitted in the >14-to-20-hour case only if the conditions of §121.467(b)(8) and (b)(9) are both satisfied (see §4 below).

In every case the rest period must fall **between the completion of the scheduled duty period and the commencement of the subsequent duty period** — it is the whole gap between duty periods, not a subset of it.

This is the federal floor. It is not a ceiling: an applicable collective bargaining agreement or company manual may (and in practice often does) require more. The CBA/manual must be checked before the number is used operationally (see §9).

=====================================================================
2. REST MATRIX (§121.467)
=====================================================================

| # | Scheduled duty period | Minimum scheduled rest | Additional conditions | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14 h or less | 10 consecutive hours | Rest must occur between completion of the scheduled duty period and commencement of the subsequent duty period | §121.467(b)(2) |
| 2 | More than 14 h, not more than 20 h | 12 consecutive hours | Same boundary rule | §121.467(b)(7) |
| 3 | More than 14 h, not more than 20 h, with reduced rest elected | 10 consecutive hours | Must be followed by a subsequent rest period of at least 14 consecutive hours, scheduled to begin no later than 24 hours after the beginning of the reduced rest period | §121.467(b)(8) |
| 4 | Any duty period during the 24-hour period commencing at the start of a reduced rest period | Duty period may not exceed 14 h | Applies whenever the carrier elects reduced rest under (b)(8) | §121.467(b)(9) |
| 5 | Any assignment | — | No duty period may be assigned unless the flight attendant has had at least the minimum rest required by the section | §121.467(b)(10) |
| 6 | Any required rest period | — | No duty may be assigned during any required rest period | §121.467(b)(11) |

Tier boundaries are exclusive/inclusive exactly as written: row 1 covers duty periods at or below 14:00; row 2 covers duty periods strictly greater than 14:00 and at or below 20:00.

=====================================================================
3. CLOCK BOUNDARIES — WHAT "BETWEEN DUTY DAYS" MEANS
=====================================================================

The regulation does not use the phrase "duty day." The operative term is **duty period**, defined in the Part 121 definitions as the period of elapsed time between reporting for an assignment involving flight time and release from that assignment by the certificate holder conducting domestic, flag, or supplemental operations.

Consequences for compliance:
- The rest clock **starts at release from the scheduled duty period** (completion of the scheduled duty period), not at the last flight's block-in and not at some notional calendar-day boundary.
- The rest clock **stops at the commencement of the subsequent duty period** (report time for the next assignment), not at the first flight's departure.
- Therefore post-flight debrief, and pre-flight report time for the next duty period, sit **inside** the duty periods and **outside** the rest period. They consume the gap and do not count as rest.
- "Duty day" as used informally by crews (a calendar day containing flying) has no regulatory force. Do not compute rest from calendar days.
- The section as written draws **no distinction between rest at home base and rest on a layover**. The 10/12-hour minimum applies identically wherever the rest is taken, for domestic and flag operations. (Any home-base/layover difference would come from the CBA or company manual, not from §121.467.)

=====================================================================
4. REDUCED REST — MECHANICS AND WORKED EXAMPLE
=====================================================================

The reduced-rest provision is narrow. It is available **only** in the >14-to-20-hour duty period case, i.e., only to reduce the 12-hour requirement of (b)(7) down to 10. There is no regulatory mechanism to reduce the 10-hour requirement of (b)(2) below 10.

Conditions, all of which must hold simultaneously (§121.467(b)(8) and (b)(9)):
1. The preceding scheduled duty period was more than 14 h and not more than 20 h.
2. The rest between the two duty periods is at least 10 consecutive hours.
3. The flight attendant is provided a subsequent rest period of at least 14 consecutive hours.
4. That 14-hour rest is scheduled to begin no later than 24 hours after the beginning of the reduced rest period.
5. The 14-hour rest occurs between completion of a scheduled duty period and commencement of the subsequent duty period.
6. During the 24-hour period commencing at the beginning of the reduced rest period, the flight attendant is not scheduled for a duty period of more than 14 hours (§121.467(b)(9)).

Worked example (compliant reduced rest):
- Duty period A: report 06:00, release 22:00 (16 h 00 m scheduled duty period — within the >14 to <=20 tier).
- Reduced rest begins 22:00 Day 1; 10 h 00 m runs to 08:00 Day 2.
- Duty period B: report 08:00 Day 2, release 20:00 Day 2 (12 h 00 m — satisfies the (b)(9) 14-hour cap because the 24-hour window commencing 22:00 Day 1 ends 22:00 Day 2, and duty period B is 12 h 00 m, at or below 14 h).
- Subsequent rest: begins 20:00 Day 2, must be at least 14 consecutive hours (to 10:00 Day 3 minimum) and must begin no later than 22:00 Day 2 (24 h after 22:00 Day 1). 20:00 is earlier than 22:00 — condition satisfied.

Worked example (non-compliant, to show the trap):
- Duty period A: report 06:00, release 22:00 (16 h 00 m).
- Rest 22:00 to 08:00 = 10 h 00 m, next report 08:00. If the carrier has **not** scheduled the paired 14-hour subsequent rest beginning within 24 hours of 22:00, this is a violation of (b)(7) — 12 hours was required and only 10 was given. A 10-hour gap after a 16-hour duty period is lawful **only** as reduced rest with the (b)(8)/(b)(9) package attached.

Plain-case example (the headline answer):
- Duty period A: report 05:00, release 15:00 (10 h 00 m — at or below 14 h).
- Rest 15:00 to 01:00 = 10 h 00 m. Duty period B reports 01:00. Compliant under (b)(2): exactly 10 consecutive hours, scheduled, between the two duty periods.
- Same duty period A with duty period B reporting 00:30 (9 h 30 m rest) is non-compliant. There is no 9-hour floor in Part 121.

=====================================================================
5. WHAT THE REST PERIOD MUST BE FREE OF
=====================================================================

§121.467(b)(11) prohibits assigning a flight attendant to perform **any duty** with the certificate holder during any required rest period. The rest period must therefore be free of all assigned duty, not merely free of flight time. In practice this means: no deadhead transportation assigned as duty, no training, no assigned ground duties, no required check-ins or calls that constitute duty, and no scheduling of the flight attendant onto another assignment inside the window.

Standby/reserve status: the fetched rule text does not address whether on-call status counts as duty or as rest for §121.467 purposes. This is governed by the certificate holder's FAA-accepted flight attendant duty and rest program and by the applicable CBA, and must be confirmed against both before it is relied on. Do not assume on-call time is rest.

=====================================================================
6. DELAYS AND IRREGULAR OPERATIONS
=====================================================================

§121.467 is drafted in terms of **scheduled** duty and **scheduled** rest, but §121.467(b)(10) is absolute: no certificate holder may assign a flight attendant any duty period unless the flight attendant **has had** at least the minimum rest required by the section. Read together:

- If actual release is later than scheduled, the next report time must move later so that the flight attendant actually receives the full minimum rest. A schedule that complied on paper does not cure an actual shortfall.
- If actual report is earlier than scheduled, the rest actually received is shortened accordingly and the same rule applies.
- The operational control point is the report time of the next duty period, not the published schedule.
- The carrier's scheduling system must therefore recompute rest on actual release/report times, not only at bid/publication time.

=====================================================================
7. SOURCE CONFLICT — 9 HOURS VS. 10 HOURS, AND WHICH TEXT GOVERNS
=====================================================================

A conflict exists in the materials reviewed and must be resolved explicitly:

- **Current eCFR text of §121.467(b)(2)** (fetched 2026-11-15): "at least 10 consecutive hours."
- **FAA public FAQ page** ("What are the flight attendant duty period and rest requirements?"): "at least nine consecutive hours of scheduled rest... our regulations allow a rest period of only eight consecutive hours."
- **§135.273(b)(2)/(b)(3)** and **§91.1062(a)(2)/(a)(3)**: 9 consecutive hours, reducible to 8.
- **2022 final rule, Flight Attendant Duty Period Limitations and Rest Requirements** (Amdt. 121-386, 87 FR 61465; docket document ARM-220928-001, 04 OCT 2022): implements FAARA 2018 §335(a), which requires the FAA to amend the flight attendant rules so that a flight attendant scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less "is given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 hours of consecutive rest."

Resolution and rationale: **I rely on the current eCFR text of §121.467(b)(2) — 10 consecutive hours.** Reasons: (i) the rule text in its current edition governs over a page that describes it, and over an earlier edition; (ii) the 2022 final rule and its statutory mandate confirm 10 is the current figure and that 9 is the superseded one; (iii) the FAQ page is a descriptive summary that has not been updated to the amended figure and, read literally, would direct a Part 121 carrier to an unlawful schedule. The 9/8 figures in Parts 135 and 91 subpart K are not stale — they are the correct figures for **those** operating parts, which were not amended by the Part 121 rulemaking; they are simply not applicable to a Part 121 carrier.

Compliance action: treat the FAQ page as a known-stale public reference and do not cite it as authority for a Part 121 rest minimum.

=====================================================================
8. REGIME COMPARISON — WHICH PART ARE YOU UNDER?
=====================================================================

| Regime | Duty period <=14 h | Reduced rest | Duty period >14 to <=20 h | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Part 121** (§121.467) | **10 consecutive hours** | 12 h tier reducible to 10 h with paired 14 h rest, 24 h window, and 14 h duty cap | 12 consecutive hours | Domestic, flag, supplemental operations — the assumed case |
| Part 135 (§135.273) | 9 consecutive hours | Reducible to 8 h with subsequent 10 h rest beginning within 24 h | 12 consecutive hours (reducible to 10 h with subsequent 14 h) | Commuter/on-demand certificate holders |
| Part 91 subpart K (§91.1062) | 9 consecutive hours | Reducible to 8 h with subsequent 10 h rest beginning within 24 h | 12 consecutive hours (reducible to 10 h with subsequent 14 h) | Fractional ownership program managers |

If the operation is in fact a Part 135 or Part 91K program, the answer changes to 9 hours and this determination must be reissued. The rest of this memo assumes Part 121.

=====================================================================
9. CBA / COMPANY MANUAL OVERLAY (CAVEAT, NOT A SUBSTITUTE)
=====================================================================

§121.467 sets a floor. An applicable collective bargaining agreement or company manual commonly requires more — e.g., a longer minimum rest, a higher duty-period-to-rest ratio, or restrictions on reduced rest that are stricter than (b)(8). Where the CBA and the regulation differ, the carrier must satisfy **both**; the more restrictive provision controls as a practical matter.

This memo states the **regulatory minimum only**. The negotiated rest language for a specific carrier was not available in the sources reviewed and is not stated here. For an airline-specific answer, the controlling CBA and the carrier's FAA-accepted flight attendant duty and rest program must be compared line-by-line against §121.467, and the answer reported as the greater of the two.

=====================================================================
10. EVIDENCE AND VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
=====================================================================

For each pairing of consecutive duty periods, the carrier should be able to demonstrate:
1. Scheduled release time of the preceding duty period and scheduled report time of the next duty period, and the resulting rest interval.
2. The scheduled duration of the preceding duty period, to establish which tier (<=14 h vs. >14-to-20 h) applies.
3. Where reduced rest was used: the paired 14-hour subsequent rest, its start time relative to the 24-hour window measured from the beginning of the reduced rest, and confirmation that no duty period exceeded 14 hours inside that 24-hour window.
4. Actual (not only scheduled) release and report times, showing the minimum was actually received (§121.467(b)(10)).
5. Confirmation that no duty of any kind was assigned inside a required rest period (§121.467(b)(11)).
6. The CBA/manual rest provision in force on the date of operation, with the comparison to the regulatory floor.
7. Retention of the above in the carrier's crewmember records; the specific retention rule and period should be confirmed against the current text of the Part 121 recordkeeping subpart rather than assumed.

=====================================================================
11. ITEMS NOT VERIFIED IN THE SOURCES REVIEWED — CONFIRM BEFORE RELYING
=====================================================================

These do not affect the headline answer but must be closed out before this determination is used operationally:

- **§121.467(b)(1) and (b)(4)-(b)(6)** were not fetched in full. The base 14-hour scheduled duty period limit and the augmentation conditions permitting duty periods up to 20 hours should be read in the current eCFR text; the 12-hour tier in row 2 of the matrix is keyed to those paragraphs.
- **Reserve/standby status** — whether on-call time counts as duty or rest is not addressed in the fetched rule text. Confirm against the carrier's accepted duty/rest program and the CBA.
- **Carrier-specific CBA rest language** — not available; see §9.

BOTTOM LINE
=====================================================================

**10 consecutive hours** of scheduled rest between the completion of one duty period and the commencement of the next, for a flight attendant on a duty period of 14 hours or less, under 14 CFR §121.467(b)(2). **12 consecutive hours** if the duty period is more than 14 but not more than 20 hours, reducible to 10 only with the paired 14-hour rest and the 14-hour duty cap of §121.467(b)(8)-(b)(9). Any CBA or company manual provision that is more protective controls in addition.
